# List item — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a list item when the data is a set of records read one at a time rather than compared across columns: a message list, a set of contacts, a search result set. The headline is the thing you would scan for and the supporting line is what confirms it. The interesting part is that the row is static until you say otherwise — passing `onPress` or `href` turns it into a real control rather than a row that merely looks clickable, which is the difference between a list a keyboard can use and one it cannot.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use the `kern.list-item.container` row height with the shape-scale gutter between rows and state layers on interaction.
- Keep supporting text and icons in their roles and sizes.

**Don't**

- Don't shrink rows below one-line metrics to save space.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Row | resting | comp.list.one-line | 56px, body-large on-surface |
| Row | hover | comp.list.hover-layer | on-surface 8% |

### FAQ

**Row or card?**

Rows for homogeneous lists; cards for heterogeneous subjects with media and actions.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a list item when you are building a list row and want the standard shape: a title, a line of supporting text, and something that happens on press. It is pressable rather than a plain view, so the row is the target rather than a small control inside it — which is how a list should work on a compact screen. `title` is required, because a row with no name is a row nobody can act on. Note that `accessibilityRole` is overridable: the default fits a pressable row, and you change it when the row plays a different part.

### Usage

**Do**

- `title` is required and `supporting` is the second line — one subject per row.
- Mark the current row with `selected`: the secondary-container fill with `16dp` corners is the whole signal.
- Rows without `onPress` are static text — no role, no stop.

**Don't**

- Don't put two actions in one row — split the rows instead.
- Don't restyle `contentStyle` past spacing — the row's `56dp` rhythm is what scans.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Row | resting | transparent | no fill — rows separate by rhythm, not paint, minHeight 56 |
| Selected row | selected | theme.color.secondaryContainer | secondaryContainer fill, 16px corners |
| Title | resting | theme.color.onSurface | onSurface 14px (onSecondaryContainer when selected) |
| Supporting | resting | theme.color.onSurfaceVariant | onSurfaceVariant 12px second line |

### FAQ

**List item or card?**

Rows in a scrolling set mean list items; one subject with its own actions means a card. A pressable card is a list item, per the card page.

**How does this differ from the web list item?**

Same contract (`title`/`supporting`, `selected` fill, static-vs-actionable rows). The accessible label joins title and supporting with a comma, and the role defaults to button only when `onPress` is set.
